column1: # NAS messages that other implementations sent, captured in a lab run on 2026-10-12.
#   sender               the implementation whose message this is, with its version and revision
#   direction            downlink (a core sent it) or uplink (a UE simulator sent it)
#   message              the name that pycrate 0.8.1 gives the plain message, which it encodes
#   security header type of the octets on the wire; 0 for a plain message
#   NAS COUNT            that the message was protected with; empty for a plain message
#   K_NASint, K_NASenc   the keys it was protected with, in hexadecimal; empty for a plain message
#   on the wire          the octets of the NAS-PDU as captured
#   plain                the message without its security header, deciphered
# How they were captured. Each core ran from its release sources in a network namespace of its
# own, and `tcpdump -i any sctp` ran in that namespace for the whole run. The other end of a
# core was a RAN and UE simulator, and that of the UE simulator below was an AMF. The procedures
# were registrations and attaches with sessions, deregistrations and detaches, service requests,
# handovers, and the rejections that a core answers to deliberately wrong messages.
# The keys and the plain messages are not this crate's work. A program of its own (MILENAGE of
# TS 35.206, the derivations of TS 33.501 Annex A and TS 33.401 Annex A, AES-CMAC and AES-CTR of
# the Python package `cryptography`, checked against TS 35.207 test set 1 and TS 33.401 C.1.1
# and C.2.2) derived the keys from each AUTHENTICATION REQUEST, verified every protected message
# with 128-NIA2 or 128-EIA2 and deciphered it with 128-NEA2 or 128-EEA2.
# The subscribers are test subscribers of PLMN 208-93 with the key of the sample configuration
# of PacketRusher: nothing here is of a real subscriber.
# - No commercial UE, RAN or core: two open-source cores and one open-source UE simulator, and
#   free5GC and PacketRusher have one NAS library family.
# - No uplink EPS message of another implementation.
# - Algorithm 2 alone (AES): SNOW 3G and ZUC were not negotiated in these runs.
# - The message types of these procedures, not all of the specifications.
